correctness.rationale: Exact exhaustive enumeration of all connected proper interval graphs through eight vertices from monotone straight-order endpoint sequences, classified up to reversal per Saitoh et al. Lemma 1; the 232 count agrees with their Theorem 1. An independent exact search over all adjacency-preserving permutations computes automorphism orbits; an exact stable-multiset refinement computes color cells. All 352 types through order eight were tested. The unique counterexample has a direct equitable degree partition and triangle-invariance orbit obstruction. A shared-palette check gives distinct signatures for all types of each order. The verifier runs to VERIFY_OK with standard Python.

originality.rationale: The published connected-proper-interval enumeration and canonical representation (Saitoh et al., 2010) do not address stable color partitions or automorphism orbits. The general notion and hierarchy of refinable graphs (Arvind et al., 2015, Sections 1 and 8) do not state the eight-vertex first failure or its uniqueness. Complete exact computation supplies the missing cutoff and a direct structural witness. Priority remains provisional because unindexed work may exist.
residual_risks: This is a finite-class classification, not a larger-order theorem.
An inaccessible or unindexed technical report may already contain the eight-vertex cutoff and unique counterexample.
The proof of exhaustive graph-family coverage relies on the published canonical straight-order theorem.

value.rationale: Refinability measures whether a widely used logic/graph-isomorphism refinement fully detects vertex symmetries. Connected unit interval graphs are a basic highly constrained class. Its first and unique order-eight failure is a natural complete cutoff, not an arbitrary slice; the obstruction separates orbit recovery from graph recognition within the class, while revealing the exact equitable partition mechanism.
